total_cholesterol.whatItIs: Measures the total amount of cholesterol in your blood. It includes both LDL ("bad") and HDL ("good") cholesterol.
total_cholesterol.ifHigh: Higher total cholesterol is linked to a greater risk of heart disease. For adults, the healthy level is less than 200 mg/dL.

ldl_c.whatItIs: LDL (low-density lipoprotein) is called "bad" cholesterol because it is the main source of the cholesterol buildup that narrows or blocks arteries.
ldl_c.ifHigh: Higher LDL is linked to a higher risk of heart disease; for adults, the healthy level is less than 100 mg/dL.

hdl_c.whatItIs: HDL (high-density lipoprotein) is called "good" cholesterol because it helps get rid of "bad" LDL cholesterol.
hdl_c.ifLow: A low HDL is considered less than 40 mg/dL in men and less than 50 mg/dL in women.

triglycerides.whatItIs: Triglycerides are a type of fat in your blood. Your body uses some for energy, but high levels can raise the risk of heart disease.
triglycerides.ifHigh: Higher triglycerides are linked to an increased risk of heart disease; 150-199 mg/dL is often called borderline high and 200 mg/dL or more high.
triglycerides.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know

non_hdl_cholesterol.whatItIs: Your total cholesterol minus your HDL. It includes LDL and other types of cholesterol such as VLDL, so it is a calculated number rather than a directly measured one.
non_hdl_cholesterol.ifHigh: A higher non-HDL is linked to a greater risk of heart disease; for adults, the healthy level is less than 130 mg/dL.
non_hdl_cholesterol.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know

cholesterol_hdl_ratio.whatItIs: The ratio of your total cholesterol to your HDL cholesterol, reported as part of a lipid panel.
cholesterol_hdl_ratio.ifHigh: Laboratories report this ratio as an index to coronary artery disease.
cholesterol_hdl_ratio.sourceTitle: Labcorp — Lipid Panel With Total Cholesterol:HDL Ratio

ldl_hdl_ratio.whatItIs: The ratio of LDL ("bad") cholesterol to HDL ("good") cholesterol, reported as part of a lipid panel.
ldl_hdl_ratio.ifHigh: Labcorp says LDL:HDL ratios are useful because a person with low LDL cholesterol but very low HDL cholesterol may still be in jeopardy.
ldl_hdl_ratio.sourceTitle: Labcorp — Lipid Panel With LDL:HDL Ratio

apob.whatItIs: Apolipoprotein B is the main protein on LDL particles. It plays an essential role in carrying cholesterol through the blood.
apob.ifHigh: Higher ApoB is associated with the development of atherosclerosis; Labcorp lists below 90 mg/dL as desirable, 90–99 as borderline high, and 100 mg/dL or more as high.

lpa.whatItIs: Lipoprotein (a) is a type of LDL particle. It is stickier than other LDL particles, so it may be more likely to cause blockages and clots in the arteries.
lpa.ifHigh: A higher level may mean a higher risk of heart disease and stroke, even if other cholesterol results are in range. It is largely inherited.

glucose_fasting.whatItIs: Measures the amount of glucose (blood sugar) in your blood. Glucose comes from food and is your body's main source of energy.
glucose_fasting.ifHigh: Higher blood glucose may be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes.
glucose_fasting.ifLow: Low blood glucose is much less common in people without diabetes and may be caused by certain medicines or conditions.

hba1c.whatItIs: Shows your average blood glucose over the past two to three months, by measuring the share of your red blood cells that have glucose attached to their hemoglobin.
hba1c.ifHigh: Higher A1C levels are a sign of higher average blood glucose and are used to screen for or monitor prediabetes and diabetes.

insulin.whatItIs: Measures the amount of insulin in your blood. Insulin is a hormone your pancreas makes that helps move glucose from your blood into your cells for energy.
insulin.ifHigh: Higher insulin may be seen with insulin resistance, where cells respond poorly to insulin and the pancreas makes more to compensate.
insulin.ifLow: A low insulin level means the pancreas is making too little, which can let blood glucose rise.

c_peptide.whatItIs: Measures C-peptide, a fragment released by the pancreas when it makes insulin. Because it lasts longer and is not in insulin medicines, it reflects how much insulin your body makes itself.
c_peptide.ifHigh: A high C-peptide usually means your body is making more insulin than it needs; it may be seen with type 2 diabetes or a pancreatic tumour.
c_peptide.ifLow: A low C-peptide may mean your body is not making enough insulin, which can be seen with type 1 diabetes.

wbc.whatItIs: Measures the number of white blood cells in your blood. They are part of your immune system and help fight infection and disease.
wbc.ifHigh: A high white cell count may be seen with an infection, an inflammatory disease, an allergy, or a reaction to a medicine.
wbc.ifLow: A low white cell count may be seen with bone-marrow damage, certain cancers, chemotherapy, or an autoimmune disorder.

rbc.whatItIs: Measures the number of red blood cells in your blood. They contain hemoglobin and carry oxygen from your lungs to every cell in your body.
rbc.ifHigh: A high red cell count may be seen with dehydration, heart or lung disease, or sleep apnea.
rbc.ifLow: A low red cell count may be seen with anemia, blood loss, kidney failure, or malnutrition.

hemoglobin.whatItIs: Measures the level of hemoglobin in your blood. Hemoglobin is the iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
hemoglobin.ifHigh: A high hemoglobin may be seen with lung disease, heart disease, sleep apnea, or polycythemia vera.
hemoglobin.ifLow: A low hemoglobin may be seen with different types of anemia, blood loss, or a lack of iron or vitamin B12.

hematocrit.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of your blood that is made up of red blood cells. The rest is white cells, platelets, and plasma.
hematocrit.ifHigh: A high hematocrit may be seen with dehydration, lung disease, heart failure, or polycythemia.
hematocrit.ifLow: A low hematocrit may be seen with blood loss or anemia.

mcv.whatItIs: Measures the average size of your red blood cells. It is one of the red blood cell indices in a complete blood count.
mcv.ifHigh: Larger-than-usual red cells may be seen with a lack of vitamin B12 or folate, or with liver disease.
mcv.ifLow: Smaller-than-usual red cells may be seen with iron deficiency anemia or thalassemia.

mch.whatItIs: Measures the average amount of hemoglobin inside a single red blood cell. It is one of the red blood cell indices in a complete blood count.

mchc.whatItIs: Measures how concentrated the hemoglobin is in your red blood cells. It is one of the red blood cell indices in a complete blood count.

rdw.whatItIs: Measures the differences in the size of your red blood cells. Healthy red blood cells are usually about the same size.

platelets.whatItIs: Measures the number of platelets in your blood. Platelets are small blood cells that help form clots to stop bleeding.
platelets.ifHigh: A higher-than-usual platelet count is called thrombocytosis and can make your blood clot more than it needs to.
platelets.ifLow: A lower-than-usual platelet count is called thrombocytopenia and can cause you to bleed more after an injury.

mpv.whatItIs: Measures the average size of your platelets. Newly made platelets are larger, so size can give information about platelet production.
mpv.ifHigh: Larger-than-usual platelets may be seen with a fast turnover of platelets, as in thrombocytopenia or certain bone-marrow diseases.
mpv.ifLow: Smaller-than-usual platelets may mean the bone marrow is not making enough new platelets.

neutrophils.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of white blood cells that are neutrophils. Neutrophils are the most common type and are the body's main defence against infection.

lymphocytes.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of white blood cells that are lymphocytes. They include B cells and T cells that fight infection and disease.

monocytes.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of white blood cells that are monocytes. They kill germs, boost the immune response, and clear away dead cells.

eosinophils.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of white blood cells that are eosinophils. They defend against parasites and are involved in allergies and inflammation.

basophils.whatItIs: Measures the percentage of white blood cells that are basophils. They release enzymes during allergic reactions and asthma attacks.

neutrophils_abs.whatItIs: Measures the amount of neutrophils in your blood, rather than only their percentage of the white cells.

lymphocytes_abs.whatItIs: Measures the amount of lymphocytes in your blood, rather than only their percentage of the white cells.

monocytes_abs.whatItIs: Measures the amount of monocytes in your blood, rather than only their percentage of the white cells.

eosinophils_abs.whatItIs: Measures the amount of eosinophils in your blood, rather than only their percentage of the white cells.

basophils_abs.whatItIs: Measures the amount of basophils in your blood, rather than only their percentage of the white cells.

alt.whatItIs: Measures the amount of ALT in your blood. ALT is an enzyme found mainly in the liver; when liver cells are damaged, they release it into the blood.
alt.ifHigh: High ALT in the blood may be a sign of a liver injury or disease, and can rise before symptoms appear.

ast.whatItIs: Measures the amount of AST in your blood. AST is an enzyme found mainly in the liver but also in the heart, muscles, and other tissues.
ast.ifHigh: High AST can occur when the liver or other cells that contain AST are damaged.

alp.whatItIs: Measures the amount of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in your blood. ALP is an enzyme found in many tissues, with higher amounts in the liver, bile ducts, and bones.
alp.ifHigh: Abnormal ALP may be a sign of a range of conditions, including liver disease, bone disorders, and chronic kidney disease.

ggt.whatItIs: Measures the amount of GGT in your blood. GGT is an enzyme found throughout the body but mainly in the liver.
ggt.ifHigh: High GGT may be a sign of liver disease or damage to the bile ducts. Drinking alcohol raises GGT levels.

total_bilirubin.whatItIs: Measures the level of bilirubin in your blood. Bilirubin is a yellowish waste product made when your body breaks down old red blood cells.
total_bilirubin.ifHigh: High bilirubin may mean your liver isn't working right, and can cause jaundice, a yellowing of the skin and eyes.

direct_bilirubin.whatItIs: Direct bilirubin is one of the forms of bilirubin a bilirubin blood test can measure; it is also called conjugated bilirubin.

albumin.whatItIs: Measures the amount of albumin in your blood. Albumin is a protein made by your liver that keeps fluid from leaking out of your blood vessels.
albumin.ifHigh: High albumin may be a sign of dehydration.
albumin.ifLow: Low albumin can be a sign of liver or kidney disease, or another medical condition.

total_protein.whatItIs: Measures the total amount of protein in your blood. It includes albumin and globulins, the two major types of protein in the blood.
total_protein.ifLow: A low total protein may be a sign of liver disease, kidney disease, or malnutrition.
total_protein.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Total Protein and Albumin/Globulin (A/G) Ratio

globulin.whatItIs: Measures the globulins, the proteins in your blood other than albumin. Globulins help fight infection and move nutrients around the body.
globulin.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Total Protein and Albumin/Globulin (A/G) Ratio

albumin_globulin_ratio.whatItIs: The albumin/globulin (A/G) ratio compares the amount of albumin in your blood to the amount of globulin.
albumin_globulin_ratio.ifHigh: An A/G ratio outside the normal range can be a sign of a serious health problem.
albumin_globulin_ratio.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Total Protein and Albumin/Globulin (A/G) Ratio

creatinine.whatItIs: Measures the level of creatinine in your blood. Creatinine is a normal waste product from muscle use that healthy kidneys filter out.
creatinine.ifHigh: A high blood creatinine may mean the kidneys are not filtering well; it can be a sign of kidney disease.

egfr.whatItIs: An estimate of how much blood your kidneys filter each minute. It is calculated from creatinine, age, weight, height, and sex.
egfr.ifLow: A lower eGFR may mean reduced kidney function; it is used to help gauge how serious kidney disease may be.

bun.whatItIs: Measures the amount of urea nitrogen in your blood. Urea nitrogen is a waste product formed as your body breaks down proteins.
bun.ifHigh: A higher-than-usual BUN may be a sign your kidneys aren't working well; BUN also tends to rise with age and can vary by sex.

bun_creatinine_ratio.whatItIs: Compares your blood urea nitrogen (BUN) with your creatinine. When the two are measured in the same test, comparing them can help find out the cause of a kidney problem.

uric_acid.whatItIs: Measures the amount of uric acid in your blood. Uric acid is a normal waste product your body makes when it breaks down purines.
uric_acid.ifHigh: High uric acid can build up in the blood and form crystals in and around the joints, a condition called gout.
uric_acid.ifLow: Low uric acid is uncommon and is usually not the main concern; the test is mostly used to look at high levels.

sodium.whatItIs: Measures the level of sodium, an electrolyte that helps control the amount of fluid in your body and helps your nerves and muscles work.
sodium.ifHigh: An abnormal sodium level may be a sign of a fluid or acid-base imbalance or another serious health problem.

potassium.whatItIs: Measures the level of potassium, an electrolyte that helps your cells, heart, and muscles work properly.
potassium.ifHigh: Abnormal potassium levels may be a sign of a serious health problem, including kidney disease or a dangerous irregular heartbeat.

chloride.whatItIs: Measures the level of chloride, an electrolyte that helps control the amount of fluid in your body and helps maintain healthy blood volume and pressure.
chloride.ifHigh: An abnormal chloride level may be a sign of a fluid or acid-base imbalance in the body.

co2_bicarbonate.whatItIs: Measures bicarbonate, an electrolyte that helps maintain your body's acid-base (pH) balance and helps move carbon dioxide through the blood.
co2_bicarbonate.ifHigh: An abnormal bicarbonate level may be a sign of an acid-base imbalance or another serious health problem.

calcium.whatItIs: Measures the level of calcium in your blood. Having the right amount is needed for your nerves, muscles, and heart to work properly.
calcium.ifHigh: An abnormal blood calcium level may be a sign of a health problem affecting the bones, kidneys, or other organs.

magnesium.whatItIs: Measures the amount of magnesium in your blood. Magnesium is a mineral that helps your muscles, nerves, and heart work properly.
magnesium.ifHigh: A high magnesium level is uncommon and most cases occur in people who have kidney failure.
magnesium.ifLow: A low magnesium level is called magnesium deficiency and is more common than a high level.

phosphorus.whatItIs: Measures the level of phosphate in your blood. Phosphate works together with calcium to build strong bones and teeth.
phosphorus.ifHigh: An abnormal phosphate level may be a sign of a health problem, often related to the kidneys, bones, or calcium balance.

anion_gap.whatItIs: A calculated value showing the gap between negatively and positively charged electrolytes in your blood, reflecting your acid-base balance.
anion_gap.ifHigh: A high anion gap may mean your blood is more acidic than usual.
anion_gap.ifLow: A low anion gap may mean your blood isn't acidic enough; it is uncommon and is often linked to a low albumin level.

tsh.whatItIs: Measures thyroid-stimulating hormone, which your pituitary gland makes to tell your thyroid how much thyroid hormone to produce.
tsh.ifHigh: A high TSH may be a sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).
tsh.ifLow: A low TSH may be a sign of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).

free_t4.whatItIs: Measures free T4, the active form of thyroxine that enters your body tissues. It is usually done with a TSH test.
free_t4.ifHigh: A high T4 may be a sign of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
free_t4.ifLow: A low T4 may be a sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).

free_t3.whatItIs: Measures free T3, the active form of triiodothyronine that enters your tissues. It is used to help diagnose thyroid disease.
free_t3.ifHigh: A high T3 may be a sign of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).

total_t4.whatItIs: Measures total T4, which is both the free and the protein-bound thyroxine in your blood added together.
total_t4.ifHigh: A high T4 may be a sign of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
total_t4.ifLow: A low T4 may be a sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).

total_t3.whatItIs: Measures total T3, which is both the free and the protein-bound triiodothyronine in your blood added together.
total_t3.ifHigh: A high T3 may be a sign of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).

ferritin.whatItIs: Measures the level of ferritin in your blood. Ferritin is a protein that binds to iron and stores it in your body.
ferritin.ifHigh: A high ferritin can be seen with too much iron in the body (iron overload), with liver disease, or with inflammation.
ferritin.ifLow: A low ferritin suggests your body's iron stores are low, which can lead to iron deficiency anemia.

iron.whatItIs: Measures the amount of iron in your blood. Iron is a mineral your body needs for growth and to make hemoglobin in red blood cells.
iron.ifHigh: A high blood iron may be a sign of iron overload (hemochromatosis).
iron.ifLow: A low blood iron may be a sign of anemia; not everyone with low iron has anemia.

tibc.whatItIs: Measures how well iron attaches to transferrin and other proteins in the blood; this is called the total iron-binding capacity.

transferrin_saturation.whatItIs: The percentage of your iron-carrying capacity that is filled with iron (transferrin saturation). It is reported with your serum iron and total iron-binding capacity (TIBC) results.
transferrin_saturation.sourceTitle: Labcorp — Iron and Total Iron-binding Capacity (TIBC)

vitamin_b12.whatItIs: Measures the amount of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) in your blood. B12 gives your body energy and helps keep your nerves and blood cells healthy.
vitamin_b12.ifLow: A low B12 can cause serious problems, including nerve disorders and some types of anemia.

folate.whatItIs: Measures the amount of folate (folic acid, vitamin B9) in your blood. Folate helps form red blood cells and make DNA.
folate.ifLow: A lower-than-usual folate level may be seen with a poor diet, malnutrition, or malabsorption, and can contribute to a type of anemia.

vitamin_d_25oh.whatItIs: Measures 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the form of vitamin D that most vitamin D blood tests measure to check your vitamin D status.
vitamin_d_25oh.ifHigh: Very high vitamin D is uncommon and is usually related to taking large doses of supplements.
vitamin_d_25oh.ifLow: A low level is associated with vitamin D deficiency, which can cause soft, weak bones.

hs_crp.whatItIs: Measures very tiny increases in C-reactive protein, a protein your liver makes in response to inflammation. This version is used to estimate heart-disease risk.
hs_crp.ifHigh: A higher hs-CRP is associated with a higher estimated risk of heart disease.

crp.whatItIs: Measures the level of C-reactive protein, which your liver makes in response to inflammation. It rises and falls with how much inflammation is present.
crp.ifHigh: A high CRP may be seen with an acute or chronic condition, such as an infection or an inflammatory or autoimmune disorder.

esr.whatItIs: Measures how quickly your red blood cells settle to the bottom of a test tube. Inflammation makes them stick together and sink faster.
esr.ifHigh: A high ESR means the cells sank faster than usual and may point to a condition causing inflammation.

homocysteine.whatItIs: Measures the amount of homocysteine in your blood. Homocysteine is an amino acid your body normally breaks down using vitamins B12, B6, and folate.
homocysteine.ifHigh: A high homocysteine may be a sign that this breakdown isn't working right or that you lack certain B vitamins.

total_testosterone.whatItIs: Measures the amount of testosterone in your blood, counting both the free and the protein-bound form. This is the most common testosterone test.
total_testosterone.ifLow: Low testosterone in men may be linked to symptoms such as a low sex drive; the test is mostly used for this in men past puberty.

free_testosterone.whatItIs: Measures only the unattached (free) form of testosterone, which is the part your body can use most easily. Most testosterone is bound to proteins.
free_testosterone.ifLow: A lower free testosterone may be linked to symptoms of low testosterone, such as a low sex drive in men.

estradiol.whatItIs: Measures estradiol (E2), the main estrogen in non-pregnant females of childbearing age. Males make small amounts in the testicles.
estradiol.ifHigh: Estrogen levels that stay too high may be a sign of a health problem.
estradiol.ifLow: Estrogen levels that stay too low may be a sign of a health problem.

shbg.whatItIs: Measures sex hormone-binding globulin, the blood protein that carries testosterone and estradiol. SHBG is made mainly by the liver.
shbg.ifHigh: Elevated SHBG can be seen in older men and in people with an overactive thyroid or cirrhosis of the liver.

psa.whatItIs: Measures the level of prostate-specific antigen, a protein made by the prostate gland. Having a low level is usual.
psa.ifHigh: A high PSA may be caused by prostate cancer, an enlarged prostate, prostatitis, or other prostate problems; the test cannot show which cause it is.

lh.whatItIs: Measures luteinizing hormone. In women it helps control the menstrual cycle and triggers ovulation; in men it signals the testicles to make testosterone.
lh.ifHigh: Abnormal LH levels may be a sign of a problem with the pituitary gland, the hypothalamus, or the reproductive glands.

fsh.whatItIs: Measures follicle-stimulating hormone. In women it helps control the menstrual cycle; in men it helps control sperm production.
fsh.ifHigh: Abnormal FSH levels may be a sign of a problem with the pituitary gland, the hypothalamus, or the reproductive glands.

dhea_s.whatItIs: Measures DHEA sulfate, a steroid hormone mostly made by the adrenal glands. Levels peak around puberty and fall as you age.
dhea_s.ifHigh: Abnormal DHEAS may mean a problem with the adrenal glands or with the sex hormones.

cortisol_am.whatItIs: Measures the level of cortisol, a hormone your adrenal glands make. Cortisol helps your body respond to stress and control blood sugar and blood pressure.
cortisol_am.ifHigh: High cortisol may be seen with Cushing's syndrome, which can be caused by steroid medicines or certain tumours.
cortisol_am.ifLow: Low cortisol may be seen with Addison disease or another problem with the adrenal or pituitary glands.

igf_1.whatItIs: Measures IGF-1, a hormone that manages the effects of growth hormone. IGF-1 levels are steadier than growth-hormone levels through the day.
igf_1.ifHigh: A high IGF-1 may be seen with conditions that cause too much growth hormone, such as acromegaly in adults.
igf_1.ifLow: A low IGF-1 may be seen with growth-hormone deficiency.

inr.whatItIs: A standardized ratio derived from the prothrombin time so that clotting results can be compared between labs and test methods.
inr.ifHigh: A higher INR means the blood is taking longer to clot; the test is used to check medicines that prevent clots.
inr.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR)

pt.whatItIs: Measures how many seconds it takes for a clot to form in a blood sample, as a check of how well your blood clots.
pt.ifHigh: A longer prothrombin time may point to a bleeding or clotting problem, or to the effect of a blood-thinning medicine.
pt.sourceTitle: MedlinePlus — Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR)

aptt.whatItIs: Measures the number of seconds it takes for your blood to clot, checking a specific group of clotting factors.
aptt.ifHigh: If the sample takes longer than usual to clot, it may mean your body isn't making enough of those clotting factors.

fibrinogen.whatItIs: Measures the amount of fibrinogen in your blood. Fibrinogen is a protein made by the liver that helps blood clots form.
fibrinogen.ifLow: A low fibrinogen may be due to the body using it up too fast or to a fibrinogen deficiency.

d_dimer.whatItIs: Looks for D-dimer, a protein fragment made when a blood clot dissolves. It is not usually found unless your body is making or breaking up clots.
d_dimer.ifHigh: A higher D-dimer may suggest a blood clot is present and that more tests are needed.

troponin_hs.whatItIs: Measures troponin, a protein found in heart-muscle cells. Normally levels are very low; if heart muscle is damaged, troponin leaks into the blood.
troponin_hs.ifHigh: A higher troponin may confirm damage to heart muscle, such as from a heart attack.

bnp.whatItIs: Measures BNP, a protein your heart releases when it is working harder than usual to pump blood. It helps confirm or rule out heart failure.
bnp.ifHigh: A higher-than-usual BNP for your age and sex may be a sign of heart failure.

nt_probnp.whatItIs: Measures NT-proBNP, a protein that is an ingredient for making the BNP hormone. Your heart makes more of it when it has to work harder.
nt_probnp.ifHigh: A higher-than-usual NT-proBNP for your age and sex may be a sign of heart failure.

ck.whatItIs: Measures the amount of creatine kinase in your blood. CK is an enzyme that helps make energy, found mostly in your skeletal muscles.
ck.ifHigh: A high CK may be seen when muscles, the heart, or the brain are damaged, leaking CK into the blood.

glucose.whatItIs: Measures the amount of glucose (blood sugar) in your blood. Glucose is your body's main source of energy and comes from the food you eat.
glucose.ifHigh: High blood glucose may be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes.
glucose.ifLow: Low blood glucose is much less common in people without diabetes and may be caused by certain medicines or conditions.

ph.whatItIs: Measures how acidic or alkaline your urine is, using a dipstick pad that changes colour with the level of acid.
ph.ifHigh: A high urine pH may be seen with a urinary tract infection, kidney failure, or vomiting.
ph.ifLow: A low urine pH may be seen with diarrhea, starvation, or a build-up of acid in the body.

specific_gravity.whatItIs: Measures the concentration of all the chemical particles in your urine. It is used to check your body's water balance and how concentrated the urine is.

ketones.whatItIs: Measures whether ketones are present in your urine. Ketones are made when your body breaks down fat for energy instead of glucose.

protein.whatItIs: Measures the presence of proteins, including albumin, in a urine sample, using a dipstick pad that changes colour with the level of protein.
protein.ifHigh: Protein in the urine may be seen with kidney disease; the test is often used to screen for kidney problems.

color.whatItIs: A visual check of the colour of your urine. The usual colour is straw-yellow; food, medicines, or illness can change it.

appearance.whatItIs: A visual check of how the urine sample looks to the naked eye, such as whether it is clear or cloudy.

nitrite.whatItIs: Looks for nitrites in the urine. Many bacteria that cause urinary tract infections change a normal chemical in urine, nitrate, into nitrite.
nitrite.ifHigh: Nitrites are not normally found in urine; their presence may be a sign of a urinary tract infection.

occult_blood.whatItIs: Looks for blood in the urine, including amounts too small to see. Blood in the urine is called hematuria.
occult_blood.ifHigh: Blood in the urine may be seen with a urinary tract infection, kidney disease, or liver disease.

leukocyte_esterase.whatItIs: A urine dipstick test that looks for white blood cells by detecting a substance they release, as a screening test for infection.
leukocyte_esterase.ifHigh: A positive test may be a sign of a urinary tract infection.

bacteria.whatItIs: A microscopic check of the urine sample for bacteria or other germs.

squamous_epithelial_cells.whatItIs: Flat cells that line the lower urinary tract and the genital area. A large number in a urine sample may mean the sample was contaminated.

hyaline_cast.whatItIs: Hyaline casts are the most common type of urinary cast: tiny tube-shaped particles seen when urine is examined under a microscope.
hyaline_cast.ifHigh: A few hyaline casts are normal; more may be seen with dehydration, strenuous exercise, or kidney disease.

bilirubin.whatItIs: Measures the level of bilirubin in your urine. Bilirubin is not normally found in urine; if it is present it may be an early sign of a liver problem.
bilirubin.ifHigh: Bilirubin in the urine may be seen with a liver or bile-duct problem.

bilirubin_indirect.whatItIs: Indirect bilirubin is one of the forms of bilirubin a bilirubin blood test can measure; it is also called unconjugated bilirubin.

adiponectin.whatItIs: Measures the level of adiponectin in serum or plasma. Adiponectin is a hormone made mainly by fat cells and is involved in glucose regulation.

leptin.whatItIs: Measures the level of leptin in your blood. Leptin is a hormone made mainly by fat cells that helps regulate appetite, hunger, metabolism, and body weight.

fructosamine.whatItIs: Measures fructosamine, the proteins in your blood that have glucose attached to them; it reflects blood glucose control over about one to three weeks.

t3_uptake.whatItIs: An indirect measure of the protein that carries thyroid hormone in the blood; it reflects the available binding sites rather than the level of T3.

testosterone_bioavailable.whatItIs: Measures free testosterone together with the testosterone attached to proteins other than sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG).
